title: CI/CD rollback breadcrumbs — canary failure investigation
summary: Scratchpad of commands tried, observed errors, hypotheses, and rollback steps during the 2025-02-14 canary instability for service-api (v1.8.4). Mostly for internal post-mortem input.
content:
Timeline + quick facts:
- 2025-02-14 09:17 UTC: Automated canary rollout started for service-api v1.8.4 (image: registry.redwood.net/service-api:v1.8.4). Canary traffic = 5%
- 2025-02-14 09:22 UTC: Alert (SLO-errors) triggered from Redwood Console: 502 spike, request timeout increase for /predict route coming from canary pods
- 2025-02-14 09:25 UTC: Observed error budget burn in canary, held at 5% -> paused further rollout manually
- 2025-02-14 09:28 UTC: Began investigation and local debugging

What I saw (logs/metrics):
- Canary pods (pod/service-api-857f9c4d) started returning 502s and 504s.
- Liveness still passing but readiness failing intermittently (kube events show "readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500").
- CPU spikes on canary pods to ~95% for short bursts (50-100ms) during requests. Old version (v1.8.3) stable at ~40-50%.
- Error logs include repeated stack traces in handler: "NullPointerException: feature_flags.get('mm') == null" (snippet below). Suspect a feature-flag gating regression in v1.8.4 build.

Error/log snippets (copied from kubectl logs -n production -l app=service-api -c api):
---BEGIN---
2025-02-14T09:21:41.123Z ERROR handler - requestId=abc123 path=/predict status=500 runtime=12ms
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.String.equals(java.lang.Object)" because "feature" is null
	at com.redwood.api.features.FeatureRouter.route(FeatureRouter.java:112)
	at com.redwood.api.handlers.PredictHandler.handle(PredictHandler.java:57)
	...
---END---

Commands I ran (notes + output summaries):
- kubectl get pods -n production -l app=service-api -o wide
  -> showed 2 canary pods + 8 stable pods
- kubectl logs -n production pod/service-api-857f9c4d -c api --since=10m | grep -i exception
  -> found NPEs above
- kubectl describe pod service-api-857f9c4d -n production  -> readiness probe failures: HTTP probe failed, reason: 500; event: BackOff
- kubectl exec -it pod/service-api-857f9c4d -n production -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -sS localhost:8080/health; echo'  -> health OK (200) but readiness returned 500 intermittently
- helm rollback release/service-api 1 --namespace production (tried local simulation on staging first)
  -> rollback succeeded on staging, but we paused for production until we had evidence
- docker inspect registry.redwood.net/service-api:v1.8.4 | jq '.Config.Labels'  -> showed build metadata: git_sha=9f3a2a4, built_by=ci-release-42
- gcloud container images describe registry.redwood.net/service-api:v1.8.4  -> image size + created timestamp OK

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Code regression: v1.8.4 introduced a feature flag path that doesn't guard nulls -> NPE under certain request shapes (most likely). Strong evidence: NPE stack traces referencing FeatureRouter.
2) Config drift: deployment manifest for canary accidentally used a new configmap version (feature_flags: v2) with keys missing -> runtime NPE. Check ConfigMap name and mount.
3) Build artifact mismatch: image tagged v1.8.4 might actually point to wrong build (old binary + new config) -> less likely but check digest.
4) Runtime resource pressure: short CPU spikes causing request handlers to timeout and fail readiness -> secondary symptom, not root cause (but increases failure amplification).

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- kubectl get configmap -n production service-api-feature-flags -o yaml  -> see which keys present. I saw the key 'mm' missing in the configmap that staging had.
- kubectl get deploy service-api -o yaml | yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image'  -> confirmed image = registry.redwood.net/service-api:v1.8.4 (digest sha256:abc123def456)
- curl registry.redwood.net/v2/service-api/manifests/sha256:abc123def456 | jq '.history'  -> verified build metadata lines, matches docker inspect.

Immediate remediation steps taken:
- 09:40 UTC: Paused the rollout in the deployment (kubectl rollout pause deployment/service-api -n production) to stop canary from increasing traffic.
- 09:45 UTC: Manually scaled down canary replicaSet to 0 (kubectl scale rs service-api-857f9c4d --replicas=0 -n production) to stop noisy pods.
- 09:52 UTC: Rolled back to previous release on production as a precaution: helm rollback service-api 3 --namespace production (release 3 corresponds to v1.8.3 tag).
  -> Helm reported release is rolled back; new pods with v1.8.3 became ready by 09:58 UTC and error rate dropped back to baseline.

Notes on rollback command specifics (for docs/postmortem):
- We used helm (charts/service-api v0.14.1). Helm history showed sequence: 2=v1.8.2, 3=v1.8.3, 4=v1.8.4 (failed canary).
- Rollback command used: helm rollback service-api 3 --namespace production --wait --timeout 5m0s
- Post-rollback validation: run k6 synthetic load on /predict for 10m -> observe 0.2% error rate, latency p95 120ms (baseline).

Follow-ups / next steps (for PM/Dev/Release):
- Engineering: revert or patch v1.8.4 branch to null-check feature flags. Quick hotfix candidate: add Optional.ofNullable(feature).orElse("") guard at FeatureRouter.route. (Assigned to Priya)
- Release engineering: tighten canary gating rules - reduce default canary to 1% and increase SLO sensitivity window from 1m to 3m for automated pauses to avoid noisy short-lived spikes.
- CI: add integration test to simulate missing feature key configmap and ensure graceful behavior (NPE should be turned into 4xx/controlled fallback).
- Ops: add alert to flag configmap key drift between staging and prod for critical feature flag maps.
- Postmortem: collect timeline and add to ENG-2345 for root cause + accountability. Draft a short user-facing blurb if customer-facing impacts found (none observed beyond internal alerting).

Lessons learned / random breadcrumbs: 
- Canary was 5% by default for this service; can amplify nondeterministic failures. Consider pre-rollout static config diff checks (compare configmap keys referenced by code vs keys present in cluster for canary).
- When debugging NPEs, check both binary and config at same time: image digest alone isn't enough (config drift is common).
- Keep helm history bookmarking consistent so rollbacks map cleanly to tags. Helm release numbers helped (we had reliable mapping here).

Raw commands to include in postmortem (copy/paste):
- kubectl get pods -n production -l app=service-api -o wide
- kubectl logs -n production pod/<canary-pod> -c api --since=15m | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl get configmap -n production service-api-feature-flags -o yaml
- helm history service-api --namespace production
- helm rollback service-api 3 --namespace production --wait --timeout 5m0s

If I missed anything, add notes here. Will escalate to Priya + release lead (Ethan) for patch + backport if needed.
